title: A pen plotter wrote the replies to a post on paper, streamed live
summary: On Sat 14 Nov at 20:02Z @samantha.wiki (977 followers) posted that a pen plotter would write replies to the post on paper, with a live stream at stream.place/samantha.wiki. The stated rules: only a person's first reply is plotted, rude replies are skipped, and replies are locked when the page fills. Replies were locked at 23:58Z, 3 hours 56 minutes after the post, and a thank-you post with a time lapse followed at 00:47Z on Sun 15 Nov. The post has 88 replies; the digest counts 43 distinct accounts replying or quoting it and 31 cluster members across the story, which is the highest-scored story of the window. During the run the maker posted the state of the queue ("half full (half empty?)" at 21:47Z; "currently EMPTY and we have 42% of the page remaining" at 22:52Z), told repliers when their turn came ("you're up"), and described a moderation check that screens replies before plotting. People replied with, among other things, the word "first", the opening of a film script cut off at the character limit, a line of code written to spawn processes without end (its author noted afterwards that it would not have run as written), a six-line poem about the plotter, and a pun. Asked how text becomes plotter paths, the maker replied "claude did 100% of this". The machine, in the maker's words, is a Genmitsu 3018 CNC machine with a 3d-printed pen plotter attachment; a post the day before showed it plotting a curve with a blue Pilot G2 0.7mm pen. Afterwards @joshuashew.bsky.social (475 followers) posted a drawing "in the style of the the pen plotter project", and the maker said more such projects are coming.

made.what: pen plotter that writes a thread's replies on paper, with a live stream

couldBeShown: A pen moving across a page writing one reply at a time, left to right, then tracking back to the left margin (a replier wrote of "the suspense while it tracks back to the left side"); a queue of waiting replies; the page filling to the point where replies lock. The maker's own images and videos carry no alt text, so research has not seen the page: its layout, the handwriting and the illustration the maker mentions are not described anywhere in the data. The only description of the look is the alt text on the follow-up drawing by @joshuashew.bsky.social (blue ink on cream paper), which is of that drawing, not of the plotted page.
numbers: 88 replies on the opening post (post counts); 43 participants (the digest's reach figure for that post); 31 cluster members in the story (digest).
Open for replies 20:02Z to 23:58Z on 14 Nov: 3 h 56 min (post timestamps).
"42% of the page remaining" with an empty queue at 22:52Z (the maker's post).
A reply reading "first" arrived at 20:03Z, one minute after the post; it is the earliest reply in the data.

Several repliers are small accounts or are not cluster members (see people: vinnymac.dev 85, robmurrish.bsky.social 139, jorropo.bsky.social 688, pds.dad 5,234); R7 applies, and each is here only for a reply the maker welcomed. Left out on purpose: a reply the maker's moderation check held back as a "vulgar insult aimed at a person", with the maker's explanation (it would show a named person's reply being rejected); two of the maker's replies whose only text is "tragic" with undescribed images (the digest keyword-flags them); one of the maker's replies that mentions an account the digest redacts as opted out; a plotted reply made of two-letter abbreviations that research does not understand; a reply that is a number spelling a crude word, and its author's later "I'm famous!"; two replies that are part of the "banh mi" bit, whose story the digest flags. The follow-up drawing by @joshuashew.bsky.social is built from 58 posts that @norvid-studies.bsky.social quote-posted; @norvid-studies.bsky.social is marked featuredPrevious: spoke, so the account is not cast to speak in this episode; its posts may be shown. The maker says the queue post would "Immortalize yourself forever on a piece of paper in my apartment": a passing mention of home, nothing more.
